stemBlocks.value: A square has side (2x − 5) cm and an area of 49 cm². Calculate the value(s) of x and hence determine the length of each side.
Think first: A square's area is the side squared, so the equation is already in completed-square form.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p107-q17 from workbook page 107.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the area equation from the diagram.
Take the square root of both sides, keeping both signs.
Test each value in the side expression and keep the one that is positive.

contentBlocks.value: x = 6 gives 2(6) − 5 = 7; x = −1 gives 2(−1) − 5 = −7, which is impossible

strategyBlocks.value: Set (2x − 5)² = 49, square-root both sides with a ±, solve the two linear equations, then check which value gives a positive side.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: x = 6 (rejecting x = −1, which gives a negative side); each side is 7 cm.

whyThisWorks.value: Squaring destroys sign information, so undoing it with a square root reintroduces two possibilities — that is where the second root comes from. Both values satisfy the algebraic equation, but only x = 6 produces a side of positive length. The check is quick because you only need to substitute into the single side expression.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing 2x − 5 = 7 only and never considering −7.

commonErrors.misconception: Expanding to 4x² − 20x + 25 = 49 and doing far more work than needed.

examTip.value: When a question asks for x and then 'hence' the length, make sure your final line answers both — the length is not the same number as x.
